rationale: The candidate reads as a single compact mass with some taper/bending cues, but the dominant impression across views is still a mostly box-like extrusion with a mild chamfered top. It is coherent in all four views, so it passes basic legibility, but it does not yet deliver a convincing public void, entry seam, or terrace response to the verified access edge. The blue frontage edge is not answered by a clearly open ground threshold; instead the building remains semantically sealed. The parcel relation is acceptable, but the dominant gesture does not strongly exploit the site boundary or access side. For neighborhood-living, this is program-adjacent but underdeveloped: the mass could support the brief, yet the active-ground and public-space invariants are only weakly expressed. The references consistently point toward courtyard, bridge, terrace, and carved ground logic, all of which are only partially present here.
